system_description.narrative_title: Trump–Xi Summit: Spectacle, Small Deals, Lingering Strategic Friction
system_description.narrative_summary: A high‑profile Washington summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping produced pageantry and a handful of limited agreements (notably a ~$30B tariff trimming and an AI dialogue) while leaving core strategic tensions — Taiwan, technology competition, rare‑earths leverage, and regional security frictions — unresolved. The event acted as a signaling and market‑shaping moment: short‑term commercial flows and business access saw bumps, but political constraints, domestic backlash, and systemic dependencies create strong feedbacks that can reverse or amplify those effects. In short, spectacle masked modest policy movement amid an open system of competing aims and tight interdependencies.
system_description.scope: The bilateral summit and its immediate ripples: U.S.–China diplomatic engagement (state visits, meetings, public pageantry), negotiated trade and tech measures (tariff adjustments, AI dialogue), corporate and market reactions (orders, supply‑chain adjustments, executive meetings), and security/diplomatic flashpoints (Taiwan, South China Sea, Iran links).
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical‑economic order: great‑power competition shaping international trade, technology governance, security arrangements, and transnational markets.
adjacent_subsystems: Global technology and semiconductor supply chains
East Asian regional security (Taiwan, South China Sea, Japan, Philippines)
Global trade and critical minerals/rare‑earths markets
U.S. domestic politics, business‑state relations, and media framing

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: Measures the frequency, prominence, and coordination of high‑level bilateral meetings, state visits, and official exchanges.

variables.name: Trade barriers level
variables.description: Measures the aggregate strength of tariffs, quotas, and other trade‑restrictive measures affecting cross‑border commerce.

variables.name: Technology cooperation depth
variables.description: Measures the extent and institutionalization of joint projects, shared frameworks, and formal collaboration in advanced technologies.

variables.name: Regulation on technology flow
variables.description: Measures the strictness, scope, and enforcement intensity of export controls, investment screening, and restrictions on technology transfer.

variables.name: Supply‑chain interdependence
variables.description: Measures the degree to which production processes, inputs, and suppliers are cross‑border integrated and mutually dependent.

variables.name: Corporate reallocation rate
variables.description: Measures the speed and volume of firms shifting suppliers, production sites, or investment across borders in response to policy or market signals.

variables.name: Critical material supply concentration
variables.description: Measures how concentrated the supply of key inputs and materials is within particular sources, affecting leverage and vulnerability.

variables.name: Strategic tension level
variables.description: Measures the overall intensity of unresolved geopolitical disputes, rivalry over influence, and strategic distrust in the relationship.

variables.name: Military posturing intensity
variables.description: Measures the frequency, scale, and proximity of military deployments, exercises, and coercive maneuvers near contested zones.

variables.name: Market sentiment (bilateral)
variables.description: Measures investor and market expectations about future bilateral economic and political relations, reflected in pricing and risk premia.

variables.name: Financial market volatility level
variables.description: Measures the magnitude and frequency of fluctuations in asset prices, exchange rates, and cross‑border capital flows linked to bilateral developments.

variables.name: Domestic political pressure
variables.description: Measures the intensity of internal political forces, public opinion, and interest‑group pressure shaping policymakers' bilateral stances.

variables.name: Signaling and pageantry
variables.description: Measures the scale and prominence of ceremonial displays, public rhetoric, and symbolic acts used to signal intent or posture.

variables.name: Policy trust between parties
variables.description: Measures mutual confidence that policy commitments, assurances, and negotiated agreements will be honored and implemented.

variables.name: Multilateral institutional influence
variables.description: Measures the effective authority and leverage of multilateral forums and rules in shaping or constraining bilateral actions.

variables.name: Cyber and espionage activity level
variables.description: Measures the frequency, sophistication, and success of cyber operations, intellectual property theft, and covert information activities affecting competition.

catalysts.title: USTR release of trade-negotiation details
catalysts.description: USTR Katherine Greer indicated details on U.S.–China trade negotiations will be released on the coming Monday, likely clarifying the scope and timeline of talks.
catalysts.rationale: “Details on U.S.-China trade negotiations coming Monday, USTR Greer says.”

catalysts.title: Implementation of $30B tariff cuts
catalysts.description: The summit agreement on roughly $30 billion in tariff cuts is expected to be implemented/rolled out over coming months as part of the extended trade truce to January.
catalysts.rationale: “China, U.S. agree to $30 billion tariff cut” and reports they extended a trade truce to January.

catalysts.title: Launch of US–China AI dialogue
catalysts.description: Leaders announced a formal AI dialogue during the summit; this is likely to become an ongoing channel for technical and policy exchanges on AI.
catalysts.rationale: “China, US agree to AI dialogue” and coverage of AI talks at the summit.

catalysts.title: Trump plans China visit in November
catalysts.description: President Trump said he would meet Xi in China in November, implying a likely high-level bilateral visit or summit in that month.
catalysts.rationale: “Trump says he will meet Xi in China in November.”

catalysts.title: Series of planned follow-up meetings
catalysts.description: Reports that Trump and Xi will meet twice more signal an ongoing sequence of follow-up high-level contacts over the coming months.
catalysts.rationale: “Trump and Xi to meet twice more after summit fails to resolve tensions.”

catalysts.title: U.S. push to restrict Chinese datacenter tech
catalysts.description: Lawmakers are moving to keep Chinese datacenter technology out of sensitive U.S. government systems, suggesting forthcoming rulemaking or legislation.
catalysts.rationale: “US lawmakers aim to keep China's datacenter tech out of sensitive government systems.”

catalysts.title: U.S. actions targeting China's critical-minerals dominance
catalysts.description: Coverage of U.S. efforts to attack China's control of critical minerals points to policy moves to diversify supply and constrain Chinese leverage.
catalysts.rationale: “See How the U.S. Is Attacking China’s Control of Critical Minerals” and coverage of rare earths dominance.
